t: You are looking at St John the Divine, an Anglican church in Kennington, in the Diocese of Southwark. It was built between 1871 and 1874 in the Decorated Gothic style, and today it is Grade I listed. The architect was George Edmund Street, a leading practitioner of the Victorian Gothic Revival who worked mainly on churches. He is perhaps best known for designing the Royal Courts of Justice on the Strand. So this Kennington church comes from the same hand as one of London's best-known law buildings.
